land.text: the settled part of the Mexican state of Coahuila y Tejas, east of the Nueces and the Medina rivers

predecessors.note: Mexico 'refused to recognize Texas's independence' and 'considered it a rebellious province during its entire existence' (Republic of Texas page).

land.text: the Republic's last shape, annexed as the 28th state on 29 December 1845

successors.note: The United States took the whole Rio Grande claim with it; the Compromise of 1850 ('in return for $10,000,000 in Federal bonds, Texas dropped claims') trimmed the claim to New Mexico.

capitals.name: Washington-on-the-Brazos
capitals.note: Interim capital in 1836 only (the Declaration was passed there on 2 March 1836); a 1842-45 stay is not on the page.

capitals.name: Austin
capitals.note: Infobox 'Austin (1839-1846)'; the Archive War 'solidified Austin as Texas's seat of government'.

rulers.name: Anson Jones
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 9 December 1844 to 19 February 1846 on the page; the Republic itself ended on 29 December 1845.

keyframe_review.note: 374,109 km2 (1836-1841). The page gives no area figure, so the infobox check is not possible; by the gazetteer the shape covers 54% of the present state of Texas, i.e. the settled east and centre. That fits the page's map note: 'the territory claimed by the Republic but not effectively controlled is in light green' and 'much of the disputed territory was occupied by the Comanche people and outside the control of either state'. The Rio Grande, West Texas and eastern New Mexico claims are drawn as a contested zone in the ledger, not as territory.

Same outline as 1836-1841 (374,109 km2). Nothing on the pages changes the controlled area in 1842: 'Woll captured San Antonio on September 11, 1842' was a raid, not a conquest, and the capital question (the Archive War) left Austin in place.

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic effectively controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 2 March 1836: Texas declares independence from Mexico. 'On March 2, 1836, delegates in convention proclaimed the Texas Declaration of Independence' at Washington-on-the-Brazos (Texas Revolution page: the declaration 'passed overwhelmingly on March 2'). The revolution itself began on 2 October 1835. The page gives no boundary; the core is Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic effectively controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 6 March 1836: the Alamo falls. 'In the early hours of March 6, the Mexican army attacked the fort'; the defenders were killed within an hour. The Mexican army holds the ground until San Jacinto.

region.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic effectively controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

ledger.note: 21 April 1836: San Jacinto. 'On April 21, Houston's army staged a surprise assault on Santa Anna'; 'Santa Anna was taken hostage; in exchange for his life, he ordered the Mexican army to retreat south of the Rio Grande.' The Treaty of Velasco 'gave Texas its independence' (no date on the page; Mexico never recognised it).

union.text: the eastern portions of New Mexico, east of the Rio Grande, that the Texians claimed

region.text: land claimed but not effectively controlled: the Nueces-Rio Grande strip, West Texas and the Panhandle, and eastern New Mexico (the Rio Grande claim)

ledger.note: 1836: the Rio Grande claim. 'Texas claimed the Rio Grande as its southern boundary. Mexico instead insisted that the Nueces River was the boundary'; 'Texian claims included the eastern portions of New Mexico, which Mexico administered'. The page dates no incident; the contest is dated from independence and runs to annexation.
1837: the capital moves from Columbia to Houston (infobox 'Columbia (1836-1837); Houston (1837-1839)').
1839: the capital moves from Houston to Austin (infobox 'Austin (1839-1846)'); the Archive War 'solidified Austin as Texas's seat of government'.

union.text: the eastern portions of New Mexico, east of the Rio Grande, that the Texians claimed

region.text: land claimed but not effectively controlled: the Nueces-Rio Grande strip, West Texas and the Panhandle, and eastern New Mexico (the Rio Grande claim)

ledger.note: 29 December 1845: the Rio Grande claim passes to the United States. The Republic ends with annexation; Mexico still insists on the Nueces and the dispute becomes the Mexican-American War (the USA dossier opens a contest on 25 April 1846).

region.text: the Republic's territory, annexed as the 28th state

ledger.note: 29 December 1845: Texas is annexed by the United States. 'Texas was annexed by the United States on December 29, 1845', 'making Texas a U.S. state on the same day annexation took effect'; Tyler signed the bill on 1 March 1845 and 'the American proposal was accepted with only one dissenting vote' (no date on the page).

wars.name: Texas Revolution

zones.text: the settled core of Texas that the Republic effectively controlled (Cliopatria's 1836 shape)

wars.outcome: Texian victory at San Jacinto (21 April 1836): Santa Anna captured, the Mexican army ordered 'south of the Rio Grande', and the Treaty of Velasco gave Texas its independence; Mexico refused to recognise it.
wars.note: Started 2 October 1835 at Gonzales, before the Republic; the Alamo fell on 6 March 1836; Cos's army 'crossed the Nueces River, officially entering Texas' on 17 February 1836 (so Mexico treated the Nueces as the limit). Reviewer 2026-10-19: clipped to the Republic's life; the revolution began on 2 October 1835 ('The Texas Revolution (October 2, 1835 - April 21, 1836)', Texas Revolution page), before the declaration of 2 March 1836.

wars.name: Rio Grande and Santa Fe claim

union.text: the eastern portions of New Mexico, east of the Rio Grande, that the Texians claimed

zones.text: land claimed but not effectively controlled: the Nueces-Rio Grande strip, West Texas and the Panhandle, and eastern New Mexico (the Rio Grande claim)

wars.outcome: Never settled by Texas: annexation passed the claim to the United States; the Compromise of 1850 'in return for $10,000,000 in Federal bonds' made Texas drop its claims to land outside its present borders.
wars.note: The Texan Santa Fe Expedition, which 'President Lamar unofficially supported', is not dated on the page; Lamar's term (10 December 1838 to 13 December 1841) bounds it.

wars.name: Mexican invasions of Texas, 1842
wars.outcome: Raids without lasting territorial result: Woll 'captured San Antonio on September 11, 1842'.
wars.note: Only the Woll raid is on the page.

certainty.note: The Republic's frontiers were claims or Comanche country, not surveyed lines: the Nueces/Rio Grande and the Santa Fe claim are the least certain; only the eastern frontier on the Sabine River, as the Texas Revolution page describes it, is firmer.

sources.title: Republic of Texas
sources.note: Identity, capitals with years, presidents with terms, the Rio Grande claim, Woll 1842, annexation 29 Dec 1845. The infobox area is not on the page as fetched.

sources.title: Texas Revolution
sources.note: Gonzales 2 Oct 1835, Alamo 6 March 1836, declaration 2 March, San Jacinto 21 April, Santa Anna's order to retreat south of the Rio Grande; no date for the Treaty of Velasco.

notes:
Cliopatria's two shapes are identical (374,109 km2, 54% of modern Texas) and are the area the Republic effectively controlled; the page's infobox area is not given, so the usual infobox-versus-shape comparison could not be made (the page speaks only of claimed-but-not-controlled land). The claim to the Rio Grande and eastern New Mexico is carried as a contested zone against Mexico (1836-1845) and then by the USA dossier (from 25 April 1846).

Pages opened (2 of 1-2): Republic of Texas and Texas Revolution. Not on them: the date of the Treaty of Velasco, the date Texas accepted the American offer, the Santa Fe Expedition's year, any 1842 capital move, an infobox area. A gap-filler should open Texas annexation and Texan Santa Fe Expedition.

Counterparts: federated-republic-of-mexico (am-08, Cliopatria 1824-1865); united-states-of-america (am-07-c; its ledger has the 29 December 1845 gain). The USA dossier dates the Texas annexation 29 December 1845 too.

Gazetteer: all names are Natural Earth or existing Cliopatria rows; the Santa Fe claim is a polygon box on the Rio Grande (approximate).
